report:
Fresh source assessment of compiler_conditions: all four ordinary implementation entries and all six ordinary associated tests are accounted for; no TODO/N/A evidence is present. The claim requires both compilers to run, independent unconditional and qualified ERROR/WARN matching, exhaustive one-to-one matching per compiler, no pooling two diagnostics against one shared marker, Sage-only snapshots, and semantic justification for compiler-condition edits.

The annotations implementation parses both severities with exactly the three allowed qualification choices, and applies_to admits unqualified markers to either compiler while restricting qualified markers. mod.rs materializes a valid fixture, executes rustc::check without propagating its result early, then opens Sage and calls observe::collect. Combining both results requires both checks to succeed. Setup-invalid fixtures are rejected before compilation; source diagnostic failures do not suppress the other compiler. observe::match_compiler_diagnostics independently filters the marker set for its compiler, matches severity and location, finds an injective assignment with augmenting paths, and rejects any unmatched marker or diagnostic. rustc::check now delegates process execution and output validation to execute/validate_output; these preserve the Rustc selector and return only unit on success. Consequently rustc text cannot enter Output: the observations, rendered diagnostics, and query trace are constructed entirely by Sage collection. The contribution instructions captured separately require semantic explanation and diagnostic investigation before changing markers; this is an authoring/review requirement, not a runtime ability to infer intent.

The complete associated test set provides: (1) only_real_line_comment_directives_are_interpreted rejects unknown, incorrectly cased, and alternate condition syntax while excluding string and block-comment lookalikes; (2) compiler_qualifiers_and_shared_counts_are_independent parses ERROR and WARN with no condition, SAGE, and rustc, then verifies zero/one/two diagnostic outcomes for each compiler, demonstrating both restricted applicability and independent counts; (3) evaluated_source_retains_blank_lines_indentation_and_unicode supplies one shared ERROR to a real source type mismatch, successfully prepares both compilers, and asserts the Sage diagnostic source text; (4) rustc_is_mandatory_and_warnings_can_be_enabled_in_source checks quiet dead-code and naming lints, rejects an unmarked rustc warning, accepts the qualified warning while asserting empty Sage diagnostic text, and accepts a qualified deny-lint error; (5) shared_markers_must_match_both_compilers explicitly rejects a shared warning missing from Sage and a qualified rustc error missing from rustc; (6) explicit_edition_and_rustc_warning_marker drives the public macro and asserts an empty diagnostic snapshot despite the matched rustc warning. The matrix would detect treating SAGE as rustc, accepting two diagnostics for a shared marker, or requiring a nonselected marker; the integration assertions would detect bypassing mandatory rustc or applying shared markers only to rustc. The unit-return boundary and Sage-only output construction also substantiate isolation of observations and queries.

Final shared-file assertion edits were inspected: the unrelated missing/unselected diagnostic tests now require the Sage diagnostic prefix, improving their specificity without changing this anchor's execution or selection semantics. No source changes were made during this refresh. This is a source review, not a claim that I ran tests on the final snapshot; root centrally executes suites. I ran review start/read/record for this anchor. No behavioral violation or missing evidence requiring edits was identified.
